A col located to the northeast will bring light to variable winds 
over the Marianas starting tonight, lifting north-northwest and 
departing the region by Saturday afternoon. A monsoon pattern that is
currently south of the Marianas will move northward over Guam on 
Friday, bringing moderate to breezy southwest to west winds and a 40 
percent chance of showers through the rest of the forecast period. 
The CNMI can expect this regime starting Saturday afternoon, so light
and variable winds and isolated showers are in store until then. 
Island-effect showers are a possibility, but the size of these 
islands tend to be too small to cause substantial rainfall. The 
forecast zones were split into two to accommodate for the timing and
spatial differences of the monsoon pattern. Isolated thunderstorms 
associated with a typically wet monsoon pattern should not be ruled 
out by the end of the weekend and through next week.

Marine...
The speed convergence associated with the surrounding southwest 
quadrant of the col to the northeast is allowing for scattered 
showers over the Marianas coastal waters, with isolated 
thunderstorms concentrated in Guam's northern to northwestern 
coastal waters and outside of the western coastal waters of Rota. The
forecast indicates these thunderstorms for Guam tonight, but may be 
re-evaluated for the CNMI as the evening continues.

Buoy data supports combined seas of 2 to 4 ft. There will be light 
to gentle southerlies for Guam coastal waters and light variable 
winds for the CNMI coastal waters tonight. Distant Super Typhoon 
Dolphin is generating a long-period easterly swell that will reach 
the Marianas Friday night, shifting northerly by midweek. Therefore, 
there is a moderate risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs at 
least through the weekend. A monsoon pattern will introduce 
increasing southwest to west winds and a building southwesterly swell
by the end of the weekend, which will most likely induce hazardous 
sea conditions to small craft vessels. Marine interests should 
monitor the forecast over the coming days as sea conditions will 
start to deteriorate by early next week.

Tropical Systems...
Super Typhoon Dolphin seems to have peaked as it moves northwest. 
STY Dolphin is centered near 16.7N 165.2E, moving west- northwest at 
13 mph. Maximum sustained winds have decreased slightly to 160 mph as
Dolphin moves southwest of Wake Island. Latest satellite imagery 
displays a well defined eye, showing that Dolphin made a splendid 
recovery from its eyewall replacement cycle. STY Dolphin remains in 
an area of favorable conditions, however, it appears that it will 
remain around this intensity for the next couple of days. STY Dolphin
is then expected to weaken starting Saturday through the beginning 
of next week.

For more information on STY Dolphin, please refer to bulletins issued
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and
by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

A weak circulation, Invest 94W, remains southwest of Guam, northeast 
of Yap Proper, centered near 12.8N 140.3E. 94W is drifting slowly
west, with little change in intensity. Invest 94W is helping to fuel
a weak monsoon surge across Palau and far western Yap State. As 94W 
continues to slowly drift west, it will maintain enhanced winds to 
the south of the monsoon trough over Palau and Yap Proper. Little to
no development is expected with Invest 94W.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough remains active across eastern Micronesia. STY
Dolphin is producing a monsoon surge across the region, producing
scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across 
Pohnpei and Majuro, with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
across Kosrae. As Dolphin continues to move west-northwest, it will
drag the monsoon trough farther north. This will allow clearing and
drier conditions to move into Kosrae Friday and Pohnpei Saturday
evening. Majuro, however, looks to remain in a wetter pattern a bit
longer, with the drier pattern moving into the Marshalls early next
week. 

The monsoon surge is now producing fresh to strong winds, making 
seas choppy and producing conditions hazardous to small craft 
operations west of the Marshalls. Therefore, a Small Craft Advisory 
was issued for Pohnpei through Saturday night and for Kosrae through
Friday night. Seas are expected to exceed 10 feet at Kosrae through
Friday night and Pohnpei through Saturday night due to a building
north to northeast swell from STY Dolphin along with a continuing
southeast swell and wind waves, especially over the northern waters.

Western Micronesia...
